title: Mount Abu and Pushkar (Batch 4)
selection: Batch 4. Mount Abu (6 sections) and Pushkar (8) get who it's for, things to do, practical info and common mistakes, refreshed overviews (pending review) and a new Mount Abu itinerary. Includes the 2026 announcement renaming Mount Abu to Abu Raj. pushkar-ajmer-2-days is left for the Rajasthan itinerary audit. Pushkar Fair length conflicts (five days vs about a week) and is flagged. Dilwara dates differ (11th–13th vs 11th–16th century); only the Wikipedia dates of the two main temples are used.

overview.text:
Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station, at 1,722 m on a rocky plateau in the Aravallis, a green, cool escape from the desert. It is also one of the most important places in India for Jains. In February 2026 the state government announced that the town will be known as Abu Raj, so you may see both names.

The white-marble Dilwara temples, the oldest built by about 1031, are famous for their carving. In town, Nakki Lake, described as India's first man-made lake, has boats and sunset views, with Toad Rock above it. Guru Shikhar, the highest point of the range, is about 300 steps up to its temple, and Achalgarh Fort lies about 26 km north. A 288 sq km wildlife sanctuary surrounds the town. Summer and winter festivals bring folk music and boat races to the lake.

overview.text:
Pushkar, north-west of Ajmer and ringed by hills on three sides, is one of the oldest towns in India. Legend says Brahma dropped a lotus here and a lake appeared, and the lake, 'Tirtha Raj', is still the heart of the town: semi-circular, ringed by 52 ghats and over 400 temples. Pushkar has the world's only temple dedicated to Brahma, and the Varaha temple, built in the 12th century, is its oldest.

Evening aarti at the ghats, a climb to the Savitri temple for the view, the 1 km market around Sadar Bazar and camel rides to the dunes fill the days. The town is vegetarian. Every October–November the camel fair, one of the world's largest livestock fairs, fills the dunes with camps.
